verdict.rationale: The evidence suggests Clerk keeps non-production and production separate: the MCP server can 'set up production instances', the CLI 'deploy' step ships auth to production, and agents can provision a throwaway accountless application with its own keys. None of it explicitly documents a sandbox or development environment whose data is isolated from production. Missing for 10: explicit docs of development/test instances isolated from production data, test users or credentials for sandbox testing, how sandbox data is kept apart from production, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Create and configure applications, manage users, and set up production instances in your Clerk workspace.
Ship your auth to production from the CLI.
